The same people are going to tell you if they don’t go good that you stink. So just do your best. Prepare to be your best and worry about being ready to go.'” COLUMBIA, Mo. − First-year coach Jon Sumrall and the No. 8 Florida Gators (4-0, 2-0 SEC) have become the center of national attention this week by going unbeaten in September. But Florida football faces another challenge Saturday, Oct. 3, at No. 25 Missouri. Off an emotional 52-28 win over Ole Miss at The Swamp, Florida has suddenly become the hunted. Upset-minded Missouri (3-1, 0-1 SEC) needs a win to keep from falling too far behind in the SEC race. Missouri has won three of its last four against UF at home. In UF's last trip to Columbia, Missouri, on Nov. 18, 2023, the Gators failed to come up with a fourth-and-13 stop late that could have won the game and instead lost 33-31 to Missouri on a Harrison Mevis field goal with five seconds remaining. A picture of former Florida defensive lineman Tyreak Sapp being taunted by Missouri players shortly after that UF loss has been shown at the UF practice facility this week for motivation. "All I'm worried about is how do we get ready to play the best we can play this week," Sumrall said, "so that's sort of the focus." picks.blurb: Staff predictions for Virginia vs Florida State — a high-end rematch on deck Skip to main content SI.COM MEN'S BASKETBALL WOMEN'S BASKETBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS BB To keep pace and maintain a tie for first place in the ACC, Virginia must conquer Florida State in its first true road game of 2026. An ACC road game is never easy — but the Cavaliers are actually favored to pick up a win at the feared Doak Campbell Stadium. Here are game predictions from the Virginia On SI staff: Jackson Caudell: Virginia 31, Florida State 21 I think this is going to be an interesting test for UVA. While FSU and West Virginia are not the same team, they pose similar challenges. The Seminoles are a mess, but they have talented running backs and a quarterback who can stress you with his legs, much like WVU. Playing away from Charlottesville has not been kind to Virginia so far this year (though a small sample size), and I think they need to be careful here. Most everyone is overlooking Florida State, but they can win this game. However, I have far more trust in Tony Elliott to go on the road and get a win to remain unbeaten in ACC play. Xander Tilock: Virginia 38, Florida State 27 At first glance, I was leaning towards picking the Seminoles at home. However, there are two major factors that make it essentially impossible for Florida State to win. The Seminoles have the ACC's second-worst pass defense through four games — so Virginia should have little trouble scoring 35-plus points. However, the other side of the ball is more important, particularly because Florida State has turned the ball over at an average greater than once per game. The Cavaliers can capitalize on those turnovers by turning them into lengthy touchdown drives. Florida State is capable of making things interesting — especially at home — but there are a few reasons why Virginia is the favorite in an ACC road game. This should be a Cavaliers win by multiple scores. Steve DeShazo: Virginia 27, Florida State 31 Saturday brings Virginia's first true road game of 2026. It comes against a proud and talented team that has not played up to its capabilities and may be competing to save Coach Mike Norvell's job in the same way I believe the Cavaliers did for Elliott last year. FSU's offensive skill trio of quarterback Ashton Daniels, receiver Ousman Kromah and receiver Duce Robinson will be a handful for the Cavaliers to contain. Beau Pribula could have a field day passing against the Seminoles, and it may be mandatory to keep Virginia close. The Cavaliers have yet to win a close game or pull out a victory away from home this season. Their only true test came at Charlotte, where the defense struggled and the offensive line showed some vulnerability in a 38-27 loss to West Virginia. Loading recommendations... Here's my Virginia vs. Florida State prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 3, 2026. Virginia vs. Florida State Pick: Virginia -2.5 My Florida State vs. Virginia best bet is on the Cavaliers to cover the spread. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . Virginia vs Florida State Odds, Spread Virginia vs Florida State point spread : Virginia -1.5 (-105), Florida State +1.5 (-115) Virginia vs Florida State over/under : 51.5 (-110o / -110u) Virginia vs Florida State moneyline : Virginia -120, Florida State +100 What a start to the season Virginia quarterback Beau Pribula is having, don't you think? He's playing to a wonderful 11-to-1 touchdown -to-interception ratio, while completing 76.7% of his passes. Do I think those numbers are sustainable? Probably not, but it's still worth mentioning. The one thing that I worry about him, though, is how often he's been sacked. Virginia's offensive line has been a sieve, ranking in the bottom 20 in sack percentage and letting opposing defenses get to its quarterbacks nine total times. And this is a team that primarily likes to run the ball. The Cavaliers are ranked 74th in pass attempts per game, while ranking eighth in rushing attempts. So, yes, there's concern there, because there's nothing spectacular about Virginia's run game. It likes to split the ball between a running back committee because Jekail Middlebrook hasn't separated himself from the pack. Middlebrook hasn't proven to be an effective distance runner, and Xay Davis and Xavier Brown clearly have the efficiency edge. On another note, I really like what the Cavs are doing defensively. They have a deadly secondary led by Jacobie Henderson and Brandyn Hillman. Hillman has already recorded three interceptions and a forced fumble. Not only that, Virginia is one of the best teams in standard down metrics, ranking second in explosiveness allowed and eighth in PPA. Its work against the pass is unsurprisingly its best attribute with Henderson and Hillman, and the Cavs rank fifth in PPA allowed and 10th in success rate allowed. Color me confused on these Seminoles. They're one of the most difficult teams to read in this Group of 6. They started off the season awfully slow against New Mexico State , despite winning, and then got into a slugfest against both SMU and Alabama. And at one point, it seemed like FSU was poised to beat Alabama for the second consecutive season, this time in Tuscaloosa. Quarterback Ashton Daniels seemed like he was lost in the pocket after the first two weeks, played a strong first half against Bama, then threw three interceptions against the Tide. The following week, he threw another pick against Central Arkansas, no less. This is a boom-or-bust team. There's a reason why the Noles have one of the most explosive offenses in the FBS, yet sit 11th in the ACC . Running back Ousmane Kromah has been a star, rushing for 6.4 yards per catch and five touchdowns. Receivers Duce Robinson and Jayvan Boggs are big-time playmakers, but because Daniels is so volatile, they can't be a big part of the offense. Defensively, this is a squad that has some active hands. Currently, 11 players have recorded a pass breakup, including two each from defensive backs Ja'Bril Rawls and Ma'Khi Jones. However, that's all the nice things you'll hear from me about their defense. Florida State ranks near the bottom in nearly every standard down metric. I'm inclined to take Virginia here. Simply, I'm riding with the better team. While this game is being played in Tallahassee, I don't think the Seminoles are good enough defensively to stop the Cavaliers. That's not to say Virginia is perfect, but because Florida State has such a hard time defensively, I see Virginia's offensive line using this game as a "get right" moment. The one concern I have with picking the Cavs is the Daniels factor. He's been known to take off and run. In Virginia's sole loss against West Virginia, the Cavs got chewed up badly by dual-threat quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr., and I can definitely see Daniels using that to his advantage. If Virginia can learn from that loss and not make the same mistakes, this is a prime opportunity to lay the points with the Cavaliers. A transfer from Missouri and Penn State, Pribula hasfound early season success with the Cavaliers. Pribula ranks in the top 10 inthe FBS in completion percentage (76.7) and touchdown passes (11) while leading Virginia to averaging 40.5 points per game. Pribulawill challenge a Florida State pass defense that allows 290 yards per gamethrough the air. That is bad enough to rank No. 135 in the FBS. In addition,the Seminoles have intercepted three passes in their four games. FloridaState defensive coordinator Tony White told the media, and by extension theVirginia coaching staff , that his team focused on stopping the run this week inpractice. We will see if that focus pays off, because the Seminole defendersare executing defensive play calls with a success rate of around 60 percent,according to White. Against non-Power4 opponents this season, Virginia allowed less than 100 yards rushing in threegames. However, against West Virginia, the Mountaineers shredded the Cavaliersdefense for 247 rushing yards and three touchdowns. So, Virginia is weakagainst the run at times. Over thepast two seasons, including a loss to SMU this season, Florida State has wonjust three ACC games, with 14 conference losses. Something has to click in themindset of the Seminoles as they come out of the tunnel and onto Bobby BowdenField. All thegood things that happened in practice this week, the execution and the focus, musttranslate into a victory for Florida State. The Seminoles must rise above theircurrent station in their football life and make the war chant and the tomahawk choprelevant again. That relevancy begins with a win on Saturday.

Trending Florida State releases updated depth chart ahead of game against Virginia: DB elevated, other minor changes Noles247.com staff predictions for Florida State's game vs. Virginia on Saturday. Noles247.com staff predictions for Florida State's game versus Virginia at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, Fla. on Saturday afternoon: Virginia's defense is a solid, though far from outstanding, unit. But in a game where possessions are going to be limited, I question Florida State's ability to slow down the Cavaliers' offense enough for Ashton Daniels and company to keep up with them, given what they've shown over the first month of the season. That starts in the trenches, where Virginia appears to have a significant advantage over the Seminoles' undersized defensive line. Even if Florida State can come out firing as they did early against Alabama , the Cavaliers will stick to what has brought them success this season and wear down the Seminoles' front as the game rolls into the second half – where they could be hurt by play action from Pribula as the second level gets antsy trying to jump into the backfield. The path to victory for Florida State comes from putting Pribula under the pressure he hasn't faced this season, forcing him into a mistake, and capitalizing with points off a turnover. But between Pribula and Daniels, the latter has been more prone to do so, and when the possession battle will be so important, one of those unforced errors could be costly for the Seminoles' chances of coming away with the victory. I think Florida State's offense will find some success, especially from Ousmane Kromah and the rushing attack. But as the game continues, the Seminoles' defense will struggle to get off the field, and Virginia will control things on the ground on its way to a win in Tallahassee. Prediction: Virginia 31, Florida State 20 I find this to be a particularly interesting matchup as both have multiple ways to win. There a lot of "good vs. bad" matchups for both teams in this game. Virginia's ability to run the ball vs. FSU's 1200 thread count soft run defense. Florida State's skill talent on offense vs. a decidedly mediocre Cavalier secondary. Etc. Etc. The position that I will be the deciding factor is quarterback. Both teams will score, and Virginia will 100% limit the overall possessions by holding onto the ball. That means the importance of every possession is magnified. Every explosive you hit carries that much more weight, but every turnover is catastrophic. It all comes down to which team plays a cleaner game and limits unforced errors. I'm taking Virginia. Prediction: Virginia 34, Florida State 27 Florida State can win this game, but I am not convinced they will. My concerns is that Virginia , led by quarterback Beau Pribula , will find consistent success running into the heart of the FSU defensive line, controlling the game, the clock, and exhausting a defense that lacks capable depth and talent. An offense with the oldest offensive line in the country can control this game and should be able to manufacture multiple clock-eating touchdown drives against a Seminole defense that leaves plenty to be desired. They are efficient through the air, though they aren't built to push it down the field aggressively. My reason for optimism when it comes to the Seminoles is that I find Virginia's defense to be susceptible. In the loss to West Virginia , the Cavaliers struggled with a quarterback who ran at them in key moments, though Michael Hawkins Jr. has more wiggle than Ashton Daniels . A couple physical backs for the Mountaineers found success, too, and I think Ousmane Kromah , who should probably see his heaviest workload of the season, can do the same. Also, Virginia will give opportunities on the outside in 1-on-1 coverage and FSU can win there, specifically Duce Robinson who will likely be very motivated after his performance, which included some tough moments, in Charlottesville last season against UVA. Finally, UVA safety Ethan Minter is a player that can be attacked on the seam or vertically with athletic wide receivers. Game can easily swing via turnovers, and that is an area where Virginia is far better than FSU at not committing them on offense and forcing them on defense. I don't have strong feelings either way with one team being an overwhelming favorite. Prediction: Virginia 31, Florida State 28 I've gone back and forth on this game. To be honest both teams are mediocre middle to bottom half of the ACC caliber teams right now. Both quarterbacks leave a lot to be desired. The skill on defense is not up to snuff with years past for either program. That being said, UVA does possess the better offensive line while FSU has the superior skill talent. What does all of that mean? Well it's going to be a battle of styles. Florida States passing attack against UVAs rushing attack. FSU must find explosive wins in the passing game at a more consistent rate while UVA tries to control the ball with a high success rate rushing attack. If Ashton Daniels can be aggressive against the man looks UVA will show him then FSU can win this game. If Ashton Daniels is passive this is going to get ugly in a hurry. I'm going to try a bit of optimism… Prediction: Florida State 34, Virginia 27 Kolby Crawford Everything is telling me to pick Virginia. Bad roster construction up front on both sides, an undersized line that can't hold up against a team built to run right at you, a season already bleeding attendance and goodwill. Which is exactly why I think Norvell comes out with a great plan and jumps on them early at home. Call it surprise, call it vibes, whatever it is, I feel it this week. I still believe this season takes a downturn fast from here, but this is one of the last wins they scrape out before it does. Slang that thing, Ashton. Prediction: Florida State 27, Virginia 23 Virginia had a promising start to the season but that loss to WVU in pretty convincing style is starting to negatively shape my perception of this team. To me the eyes test doesn't bear out against the advanced analytics. F+ has them as a top 25 defense and not a top 25 offense. That doesn't really track with what I see. Their offense is plodding and efficient. They use their mobile QB well, get their 3-4 yards a pop with a well structured IZ scheme, and then work for shots over the top off of play action. Think our offense from last year but without Duce and maybe a more consistent QB. Their defense struggled against WVU. To be honest, they looked good against NCSU but my middle school flag football team could look good against a Dave Doeren offense. Their secondary seems a bit slow and I think if you can spring into the second level you can rip off some chunks. They have a solid front six though which they try to lean on but I think FSU can find some success getting Duce and Kromah outside. This will be a dog fight in my estimation but I gotta give the benefit to the QB I trust more. away.headline: Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan
away.blurb: The Seminoles essentially have to win this weekend versus the Virginia Cavaliers to get their season back on track. Mike Norvell is coaching for his job, and the only real way to do that is by essentially winning out in ACC play. This is an extremely daunting task, but the only way to eat an elephant is by taking it one bite at a time, and that is exactly what the game will be. Now that the injury reports have gone up for the matchup , it is easier to determine how this game will look. While both teams have a number of key players out, the focus for Florida State fans should be on the losses for Virginia on their defensive line. The biggest name to look for in that area is defensive tackle Jason Hammond. Hammond entered the season as one of the players with the most hype on the Virginia defensive front. This was supposed to be the year when Hammond finally took those next steps and solidified himself as one of the better linemen in the conference, but now it appears his return this season is in question. Kromah appears poised to remain the bell cow and should mostly see the opposing starters, but Wisner is where the lack of depth for Virginia will start to show itself. As the Cavaliers start to sub players out, FSU will try to spell Kromah with the equally-capable Wisner, and that is where FSU will need to force their will on a depleted opponent. The Wisner hype was perhaps a little too premature coming into the season based on his limited reps leading up to last week, but he has an easy path towards showing why the Seminoles put so much faith in him with a nice chunk of money on the transfer market. Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan Skip to main content Recruiting In the world of college football, teams will take whatever they can get if that gives them a chance to win. This is especially the case for a team like Florida State. Hammond absolutely leaves a hole on defense for the Cavaliers and his loss is further felt by the loss of depth across the front. Devon Baxter is the next most notable name to miss this weekend, largely a backup on the season, but several other depth players are also missing, leaving the Virginia rush defense susceptible. The good news for FSU is that their rushing attack is one of their biggest strengths, and Ousmane Kromah and Tre Wisner are more than up to the task . This game will still probably have some uphill sledding for the Noles to overcome, but this does at least display the obvious path for an FSU win and earn its first ACC win of the season. home.headline: Updated week 5 injury report adds to a growing issue within Florida State's defense
home.blurb: Florida State linebacker Noah LaVallee was downgraded from probable to out after there was previously hope he would play in Week 5. The Seminoles will be without four linebackers after the LaVallee announcement, as the freshman will join Izayia Williams, Blake Nichelson, and Daylen Green on the sidelines this week. Noah's brother and fellow linebacker, Caleb, is currently listed as probable for the upcoming game. Florida State's linebacker depth just took another hit with Noah LaVallee downgraded to out for Week 5 Florida State entered the game with a handful of players already confirmed to be out of the Week 5 game, but losing LaVallee particularly stings since he is a player filling in due to the injuries. LaVallee did not record any stats through the first three games, but began to work into the rotation against Central Arkansas with 21 snaps. The injury list is still rather long, even with a handful of players removed. Defensive back Quindarrius Jones and Caleb LaVallee are still listed as probable for the upcoming game against Virginia. Florida State and Virginia both released lengthy injury reports ahead of the Week 5 battle on Saturday. Both teams will be without a good chunk of the roster, but the key difference is that the Seminoles will be without multiple players at a vital position, and another player from the same position just joined that list. 2026 has not been the most productive season up to this point for Florida State, with a handful of players powering through bumps and bruises to compensate for the number of more serious injuries, particularly on defense. Starting safety Ashlynd Barker has been playing through a broken bone in his arm, although somewhat controversially , to make up for the shocking injury total. Without Noah and potentially Caleb in the picture, the slack will need to be picked up by the likes of Karon Maycock and AJ Cottrill. Maycock, a freshman, saw his first real action of the season against Central Arkansas and recorded three total tackles. Cottrill, on the other hand, saw action against SMU and Central Arkansas, totaling two tackles. During the Week 3 game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa, Florida State only played four linebackers and opted to use plenty of defensive backs. With Mikai Gbayor, Chris Jones, and Omar Graham Jr. all expected to play in Week 5, the Seminoles' staff might just give the remaining snaps at linebacker to the more experienced Cottrill. The only issue, however, is that Alabama and Virginia are far different teams in terms of how the offense attacks opposing defenses. Virginia is going to look to keep the football on the ground for most of the game. When combined with the play-action heavy passing attack, the Seminoles' linebackers could tire easily, which will force more of the remaining depth into the game. home.headline: Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan
home.blurb: The Seminoles essentially have to win this weekend versus the Virginia Cavaliers to get their season back on track. Mike Norvell is coaching for his job, and the only real way to do that is by essentially winning out in ACC play. This is an extremely daunting task, but the only way to eat an elephant is by taking it one bite at a time, and that is exactly what the game will be. Now that the injury reports have gone up for the matchup , it is easier to determine how this game will look. While both teams have a number of key players out, the focus for Florida State fans should be on the losses for Virginia on their defensive line. The biggest name to look for in that area is defensive tackle Jason Hammond. Hammond entered the season as one of the players with the most hype on the Virginia defensive front. This was supposed to be the year when Hammond finally took those next steps and solidified himself as one of the better linemen in the conference, but now it appears his return this season is in question. Kromah appears poised to remain the bell cow and should mostly see the opposing starters, but Wisner is where the lack of depth for Virginia will start to show itself. As the Cavaliers start to sub players out, FSU will try to spell Kromah with the equally-capable Wisner, and that is where FSU will need to force their will on a depleted opponent. The Wisner hype was perhaps a little too premature coming into the season based on his limited reps leading up to last week, but he has an easy path towards showing why the Seminoles put so much faith in him with a nice chunk of money on the transfer market. Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan Skip to main content Recruiting In the world of college football, teams will take whatever they can get if that gives them a chance to win. This is especially the case for a team like Florida State. Hammond absolutely leaves a hole on defense for the Cavaliers and his loss is further felt by the loss of depth across the front. Devon Baxter is the next most notable name to miss this weekend, largely a backup on the season, but several other depth players are also missing, leaving the Virginia rush defense susceptible. The good news for FSU is that their rushing attack is one of their biggest strengths, and Ousmane Kromah and Tre Wisner are more than up to the task . This game will still probably have some uphill sledding for the Noles to overcome, but this does at least display the obvious path for an FSU win and earn its first ACC win of the season. The second half was a complete 180, as Kentucky shut out South Alabama and pulled away for a 45-21 victory, and the victory improved Kentucky to 3-1 overall and 1-1 in SEC play. Now, the Wildcats will take on a struggling South Carolina team on the road. The last time Kentucky was on the road, the Wildcats defeated then-No. 9 Texas A&M, 31-21, in College Station. The victory showed how strong Kentucky's defense can be while also giving quarterback Kenny Minchey an opportunity to show what he can become as he continues to develop under first-year head coach Will Stein. South Carolina Gamecocks (2-2, 0-2) The Shane Beamer era is facing increased pressure in Columbia, as South Carolina enters the matchup on a seven-game SEC losing streak. The Gamecocks' last SEC victory came against Kentucky on Sept. 27, 2025, when South Carolina defeated the Wildcats 35-13. South Carolina opened the 2026 season with a dominant 57-0 victory over Kent State, but the Gamecocks have since struggled against SEC competition. South Carolina lost 41-34 at home to Mississippi State before falling to Alabama 49-18 on the road this past weekend. The loss to Alabama dropped the Gamecocks to 0-2 in SEC play. Now, Kentucky comes to Columbia, making this a potentially significant game for Beamer and the Gamecocks. Kentucky is also looking to snap a four-game losing streak against South Carolina. Doing so under Stein would give the Wildcats another significant road victory during his first season. South Carolina will also be without star EDGE Dylan Stewart, who has been suspended indefinitely by Beamer and more than likely will not play against Kentucky. Stewart's suspension came after the Gamecocks' loss to Alabama, during which he threw a punch at Alabama tight end Josh Ford and had a heated interaction with South Carolina's coaching staff. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers remains one of South Carolina's biggest offensive weapons. The dual-threat quarterback opened the season with 270 passing yards and three touchdowns in the Gamecocks' win over Kent State. Wide receiver Nyck Harbor is another player Kentucky will need to account for. Harbor returned to South Carolina for the 2026 season alongside Sellers and remains one of the team's most important receiving threats. Junior running back Matt Fuller is also a name to watch in the South Carolina backfield after showing his ability as both a runner and receiver. ESPN gives Kentucky a 42.1% chance of winning. My Early Prediction: Kentucky has already proven it can win on the road after defeating then-No. 9 Texas A&M. Why can't the Wildcats do it again? South Carolina is on a seven-game SEC losing streak and will be without Stewart, while Kentucky enters the matchup ranked No. 24 in the AP Top 25 and coming off a dominant second half against South Alabama. Kentucky also has plenty of motivation to snap its four-game losing streak against the Gamecocks. Why not us? Final Score: Kentucky 34, South Carolina 27.

picks.blurb: Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus CFB Week 5 live updates Judge not on ALDS roster NFL Week 4 injury tracker WNBA semifinals preview MLB Division Series preview Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Fri, October 2, 2026 at 5:31 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kentucky Wildcats have to go on their second road trip of the season as the will face off against South Carolina at 4:15 P.M. ET on Saturday. We have previewed both South Carolina offense and defense, as well as laying out Kentucky's path to victory in this game. This is a massive game for both teams; Kentucky is trying to snap a four game losing streak against the Gamecocks and South Carolina is a desperate trying to turnaround their season. In this article, I will give my final thoughts on the game and a prediction. Kentucky has to win early downs in this game, and they have consistently done that all season on both sides of the football. Kentucky's offense has stayed ahead of schedule consistently and haven't needed to rely on converting third downs, which has been a weak spot for this offense. Kentucky's offensive line has improved every week and they have to dominate the line of scrimmage in this game. They have been phenomenal in run blocking as they lead the country in yards before contact per rush attempt, and they should keep Kenny Minchey clean as South Carolina is without their game-wrecking edge defender Dylan Stewart. Defensively, Kentucky has performed similarly as the offense. They are struggling on third downs, but they have been exceptional on early downs. If they can slow down this South Carolina run game and keep their offense off schedule, it should bode well for the Wildcats defense. Kentucky will probably have a similar defensive gameplan that they had against Texas A&M, contain LaNorris Sellers on the ground and force him to beat you with his arm. Sellers has struggled this season, he has turned the ball over four times. The turnover margin has been the downfall of Kentucky in this series as of late, as the Wildcats have 14 total turnovers in the last five matchups against the Gamecocks. That could flip on Saturday, Kentucky is +3 in the turnover margin on the season, whereas South Carolina is -4 in the turnover margin. Kentucky has done a great job at taking care of the football and creating turnovers on defense. South Carolina has their backs against the wall, head coach Shane Beamer is on a scorching hot seat. They have struggled against SEC opponents and the talk surrounding their program has been extremely loud this week. Combine that with your best player serving a suspension, it will be a lot to overcome for the Gamecocks. Who gets off to a hot start could be the determining factor in this football game. Speaking of hot starts, there are multiple reasons it could play a factor in this game. South Carolina needs to create that early momentum to keep the crowd involved. If Kentucky gets off to a hot start and the Gamecocks struggle offensively, you could see the boo birds come out in Columbia from this fan base. It is worth noting, Kentucky ranks third in the SEC this season in time trailing this season, as the Wildcats have only spent a total of over 26 minutes trailing through the first month of play. Kentucky has been good at getting off to quick starts this season, and I could see that continue on Saturday. Kentucky has a unique offensive scheme that will force a struggling South Carolina defense to communicate. Over the last five meetings, the Wildcats have averaged just 13 points per game, which is the main reason they have been 1-4 over that stretch. I believe Kentucky gets the offense going and South Carolina fails to overcome all the noise surrounding the team this week. Prediction: Kentucky 34, South Carolina 24 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction

Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will look to justify its No. 24 ranking at South Carolina on Saturday. The Wildcats are ranked for the first time in almost three years, but if they don't snap a four-game losing streak to the Gamecocks, the stint in The Associated Press Top 25 will not last long. Will Stein's squad has already proven capable of winning in a raucous road environment at Texas A&M, but Stein has been clear he does not believe UK's performance in a win over South Alabama last week was up to the program's standard. Can Kentucky build momentum in advance of a homecoming game against LSU? Can Stein flip the script in a series that has often gone a long way in determining the success of each team's season? Here is what you need to know ahead of the matchup . Kentucky cracked the AP Top 25 for the first time since October 2023 this week but remains in the "others receiving votes" portion of the Coaches Poll. That distinction offers a glimpse at the work the Wildcats still need to do to earn national respect. Upsetting Texas A&M put UK in the spotlight for a week, but now there are real questions about how good the Aggies are. Combine the sluggish opening to the win over South Alabama, and Kentucky's hold on a spot in the Top 25 appears tenuous. "It's cool and all, but I mean that thing shifts every single day," offensive guard Tegra Tshabola said. "We keep focusing on that, we won't be in there long." A win at South Carolina might not move the needle much in terms of national perception since the Gamecocks are 0-2 in SEC play, but it would at least ensure Kentucky remains ranked for its homecoming matchup against LSU next week. Despite UK's spot in the top 25, South Carolina is a three-point favorite as of Friday morning. "I think it's more important for the fans than anything," Stein said. "Our guys got to go play well. I'm not really sure why they rank people this early in the season. There's a lot of games left. It's about playing well on Saturdays. Not letting that dictate how we play. We should play to our standard regardless." Kentucky defensive lineman Kahlil Saunders (92) tries to wrap up South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers (16) during a game at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia, S.C., on Saturday, Sept. 27, 2025. (Ryan C. Hermens/rhermens@herald-leader.com) Another test for UK defense South Carolina was blown out 49-18 at Alabama last week but averaged 45 points per game in its first three games. That stretch included a 41-34 loss to Mississippi State. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers entered the season as a top-50 NFL draft prospect, according to The Athletic, but his performance has been mixed so far. Through four games, Sellers has completed 62.1% of his passes for 833 yards, six touchdowns and four interceptions. He has also rushed for 244 yards and one touchdown on 36 carries. Sellers' stats are boosted by his performance in the season-opening 57-0 win over Kent State in which he completed 19 of 23 passes for 270 yards and three touchdowns. In two SEC games, Sellers has thrown three touchdowns and three interceptions. He also completed just 10 of 23 passes for 96 yards in the Week 2 blowout of Towson but did rush for 119 yards in that game. "I think he's extremely dynamic," Stein said. "He can make every single throw. Big arm, and then when he pulls the ball down, he's very dangerous. They also have really good skill players on offense, so it'll be a big task for our defense to go against these guys, especially in their place." Sellers has given Kentucky fits the last two seasons, completing 21 of 28 passes for 319 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. He rushed for 81 yards on 14 carries last season. Kentucky football injury report Stein downplayed any long-term concerns about UK players who picked up injuries in recent weeks, but the Wildcats will be without at least one key player in Columbia. Junior wide receiver DJ Miller, who was injured while trying to run a deep route against South Alabama, was initially listed as doubtful on the SEC availability report then downgraded to out on Friday. Long snapper Cole Marszalek, backup cornerback Grant Grayton, offensive guards Jay Clark and Aba Selm and linebacker Tavion Wallace were also listed as out Fifth-year linebacker Alex Afari was also listed as unavailable Friday after the Kentucky Court of Appeals dismissed the temporary injunction that had made him and dozens of other athletes eligible in their lawsuit against the NCAA for a fifth season of eligibility. The good news for UK is star defensive tackle Tavion Gadson, who missed the South Alabama game, was not included on the availability report, signalling he is expected to play at South Carolina. Kentucky vs. South Carolina prediction A fast start could be particularly important Saturday with frustrations high among South Carolina fans. If Kentucky can take control of the game early, the atmosphere could grow tense for Shane Beamer and Gamecocks players. A high-scoring affair seems likely, but Kentucky's experience at Texas A&M should help prepare the Wildcats for the moment. Kentucky 35, South Carolina 28. The last word "I don't know a stadium in this league that's not going to be loud. … I would imagine every stadium we go into is going to have crazy fans that are really passionate and make third downs and fourth downs really difficult on the opposing offense. So, it goes back to how do you play good football? Learn how to not beat yourself before you go in. Have to be elite in communication, in operation, in and out of huddles. No huddles, cadence, all that stuff is going to be critical for our success. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for When the South Carolina Gamecocks Take on Kentucky
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for When the South Carolina Gamecocks Take on Kentucky - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus CFB Week 5 live updates Judge not on ALDS roster NFL Week 4 injury tracker WNBA semifinals preview MLB Division Series preview Three Bold Predictions for When the South Carolina Gamecocks Take on Kentucky Sep 26, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; South Carolina Gamecocks quarterback LaNorris Sellers (16) calls for the snap during the first quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alex Joyce Fri, October 2, 2026 at 6:17 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Despite all the troubles from the last two weeks, South Carolina has a chance to get the train back on the track against Kentucky. For a team desparately needing a win, here are three bold predicitions for the Gamecocks that will ultimately end their 2-game skid this season. Usually we try to give you at least one on each side of the ball, however this week we're changing things up. This is an all offense version of bold predictions. We will focus on LaNorris Sellers, the passing game, and the tailbacks. Passing Game looks smooth again It certainly won't be easy. Though Knetucky's "stats" place them in the bottom half of SEC defenses in the passing category, it doesn't tell the full story. In two SEC games the Wildcats held Alabama's Keelon Russell to 188 yards passing and Texas A&M's Marcel Reed to 236 yards. They also lead the conference in interceptions with 6. What gives me confidence in this specific matchup will be South Carolina's ability to run the ball (more on that later). A good run game can open passing windows for an offense that has struggled in that department for the last two weeks. I expect this to be the case and for Gamecocks to see a better attack than they have in recent weeks. Sep 19, 2026; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; South Carolina Gamecocks wide receiver Mazeo Bennett Jr. (3) attempts to get around Mississippi State Bulldogs safety Isaac Smith (2) in the second quarter at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LaNorris Sellers finishes with no interceptions In the last three games, Sellers has four interceptions , two of which came against Mississippi State. On the other side, Kentucky has been great this season at creating turnovers. On paper this is a matchup that favors the Wildcats. However I believe Seller ends his interception streak this week and keeps this passing game on track. Gamecocks rush for 200+ In their two SEC games this season, Kentucky gave up 155 yards and three touchdowns to Bama. Against Texas A&M they gave up 187 yards and two touchdowns. This is a front seven that can be run on and that's exactly what this Gamecocks' offense does best. Matt Fuller leads a rushing attack that is ranked first in the conference with 262 yards per game. Fuller gained 112 yards on the ground last week as the team put up 216 yards total on Alabama. Against Mississippi State running backs totaled 149 yards. That's good enough for 182.5 yards per game through two contests. Fuller should have his third 100 yard rushing performance of the season which will propel the Gamecocks to a win. away.headline: Initial Injury Report for Kentucky at South Carolina
away.blurb: A big name on the injury report is wide receiver DJ Miller, who is dealing with a soft tissue injury that caused him to just play eight snaps against South Alabama. He is listed as doubtful. Miller had a breakout game against Texas A&M and has been the second best wideout behind true freshman Kenny Darby. He has dealt with soft tissue injuries throughout his young career at Kentucky, he was sidelined last season as a true freshman because of it and dealt with something similar this offseason as well. This is certainly something to monitor. Other than Miller, Jordan Castell is the other starter listed, but he is probable, so not a big worry. Ty Bryant, the other starting safety, isn't listed on the report despite dealing with a shoulder injury over the past few weeks. Outside of Dylan Stewart serving a suspension, South Carolina is pretty healthy across the board. There aren't many notable names on this list for the Gamecocks. Defensive lineman Gabriel Brownlow-Dindy is questionable, and the other potential key player out of action. Kentucky could be slightly undermanned in this road test that is a massive game for both teams. These injury reports will continue to be updated throughout the week, but the initial injury report suggests Kentucky could potentially be down a couple key starters on Saturday. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, September 29, 2026 at 5:22 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One of the biggest ACC games of the season takes place Saturday night as No. 4 Miami heads to Death Valley to take on Clemson . Miami enters 4-0 and 2-0 in the ACC, while Clemson sits at 3-1 and 2-0 in conference play. The Tigers have won three straight since getting embarrassed 51-10 by LSU in the opener, including a 24-10 road win over Cal last week. But Clemson hasn't faced anything quite like this Miami team since that LSU disaster. The Hurricanes are averaging 51.8 points and 588.8 yards per game , ranking first nationally in total offense. Even scarier, Miami's defense is allowing only 9.0 points and 224.5 yards per game . How Miami Wins It starts with Darian Mensah . Mensah has been ridiculously efficient this season. He completed 23 of 27 passes for 338 yards and three touchdowns in Miami's 52-3 win over Central Michigan, pushing his season completion percentage to an absurd 88.7% . Miami needs to let Mensah attack Clemson early and take the crowd out of the game. Malachi Toney gives him an elite weapon on the outside, while the Hurricanes have enough balance on the ground to prevent Clemson from simply sitting back against the pass. Defensively, the formula is simple: make Clemson throw the football. The Tigers are averaging only 156.3 passing yards per game, while Miami enters with the nation's No. 1 rushing defense at just 39.5 yards allowed per game. If Miami shuts down Clemson's rushing attack early, this matchup could become extremely uncomfortable for the Tigers. How Clemson Wins Clemson needs Death Valley to become a factor immediately. The Tigers cannot afford to get into a shootout with Miami. They need long possessions, a strong rushing performance from Gideon Davidson and at least a couple of turnovers from their defense. Davidson is coming off 159 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Cal , and Clemson will likely need another big performance from him to keep Mensah standing on the sideline. If Clemson falls behind by multiple scores and is forced to throw its way back into the game, Miami has a massive advantage. I think Clemson makes this interesting early. It's a Saturday night game in Death Valley, Clemson has won three straight and the Tigers' defense has shown significant improvement since that LSU embarrassment. But Miami is simply playing at a different level right now. Mensah eventually starts finding holes in the Clemson defense, Miami takes away the Tigers' running game and the Hurricanes begin pulling away in the second half. Clemson has improved, but Miami looks like a legitimate College Football Playoff and national championship contender. (Patrick Breen/The Republic) 1 / 29 Tait Reynolds, Clemson football freshman quarterback for Dabo Swinney Tait Reynolds, Clemson football freshman quarterback for Dabo Swinney How much of this game will have to be decided by Reynolds, who is a freshman? This is one heck of a spotlight for just his third start. The Tigers have done their best to alleviate pressure on him with their run game, but Miami leads the ACC with 39.5 rushing yards allowed per game. Clemson may give Gideon Davidson carry after carry, but there will be a time when the Tigers need some big passing plays. Reynolds doesn't have to be Superman, but he has to show some growth. Can he? The combination of a still-developing freshman and an offensive line that's been so-so in pass protection plays into Miami's hands, especially with how much pressure the Hurricanes have been getting on quarterbacks. Clemson is still figuring things out with Reynolds, while Miami has a quarterback with no questions. Darian Mensah will look to do what he did last season at Duke and pick Clemson apart. The Tigers have a strong secondary, but it'll be their toughest challenge yet. Even if Mensah has an off day, the Hurricanes have a strong rushing attack that's gained over 120 yards in all four games. Miami is most likely to have a balanced offense, and it also doesn't have a clear weakness on defense. Clemson's rushing defense struggled against LSU and North Carolina, and while it did better against California, the Golden Bears are averaging an ACC-worst 101.5 rushing yards per game. Clemson vs. Miami scouting report Where Clemson has an advantage: Miami hasn't faced a secondary as good as Clemson's. Ashton Hampton leads the ACC with five pass breakups, and Elliot Washington II is tied for second with three interceptions. Getting Corian Gipson back at nickel would only strengthen an already sound unit. Clemson's secondary will have its hands full though. Mensah has been the nation's most efficient and accurate quarterbacks. But the Tigers are well-equipped to meet the challenge, just like they did against Cal's Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele . Where Miami has an advantage: The Hurricanes look better at the line of scrimmage. Miami ranks second in the ACC with 227.5 rushing yards per game, and running backs Javian Mallory and Mark Fletcher Jr. are averaging 9 and 6.5 yards per carry, respectively. Every picker who weighed in on Saturday night's matchup at Memorial Stadium chose No. 4 Miami, leaving the Tigers with a unanimous prediction to challenge in front of their home crowd. Desmond Howard, Nick Saban, Pat McAfee and celebrity guest picker Caitlin Clark all selected the Hurricanes . While the picks were the same, Saban offered the strongest prediction about how the game would unfold. "I'm all in on Miami," Saban said. "I think they're one of the most complete teams in the country so far this year, and I think they're going to dominate Clemson ." The Tigers enter the matchup with three consecutive wins and a chance to put their season-opening loss at LSU further behind them. Clemson is 3-1 overall and 2-0 in ACC play, while Miami arrives unbeaten at 4-0 with two conference victories of its own. Howard pointed to Miami's personnel as the difference, even with injuries affecting the Hurricanes. "I think Miami just has too much talent," Howard said. McAfee's reasoning centered on the offense Clemson will have to slow down. He highlighted Malachi Toney and quarterback Darian Mensah, noting that Mensah has thrown more touchdown passes than incompletions through the opening month. "We're already a month into this thing. That is a crazy stat," McAfee said. He expects Miami coach Mario Cristobal's team to deliver another convincing performance. "I will take the Miami Hurricanes to get a big win over Clemson," McAfee said. Clark, the Indiana Fever guard and former Iowa standout, also backed Miami to complete the sweep. Kirk Herbstreit did not make a pick because he will call the game alongside Chris Fowler on ABC. picks.headline: Miami vs. Clemson final score predictions: Will the Hurricanes continue their dominant start, or can the Tigers pull their season out of the fire?
picks.blurb: Miami vs. Clemson final score predictions: Will the Hurricanes continue their dominant start, or can the Tigers pull their season out of the fire? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus CFB Week 5 live updates Judge not on ALDS roster NFL Week 4 injury tracker WNBA semifinals preview MLB Division Series preview Sam Navarro-Imagn Images; Ken Ruinard-Imagn Images Craig Smith, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 1, 2026 at 2:23 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Canes and Tigers will have the eyes of the nation on them on Saturday night in a big game for two programs going in different directions. The Miami Hurricanes and Clemson Tigers square off on Saturday night in Death Valley in a game with significant ACC title implications, with the game being shown in primetime on ABC. The Canes have surged to a 4-0 start, with only a slight flutter in the second half at Wake Forest after leading 31-7 being their only show of mortality thus far. Meanwhile, Clemson has improved to 3-1 after a season-opening 51-10 loss at LSU. Lifeless performances against Georgia Southern and in the first half against UNC have turned into a come from behind win over the Tar Heels and an impressive 24-10 win at Cal last weekend. Can the Tigers ride that modest improvement into an upset win on Saturday night? Our college football writers weighed in with their game predictions. Miami 38, Clemson 28 I think the writing is on the wall for Clemson and Dabo Swinney. The program is a shell of itself, esepcially from a talent acquisition standpoint. Things are the exact opposite for the Hurricanes, as they were less than 70 yards away from a national championship. Even so, I expect Clemson to show out for this game almost as a last ditch effort to save their season. It won't be enough, as the Hurricanes prove to be too explosive for the Tigers. Tyler Forness , A to Z Sports Florida Miami 30, Clemson 10 This game had the potential to be one of the better matchups in the ACC this season if Clemson held up their end of the bargain, but it looks like Dabo and the boys have only fallen further down the list in terms of program competence. The quarterback position is a mess, and a lot of the notable draft prospects heading into the season simply haven't played up to the offseason hype. On the other hand, you have a Miami team with not only one of the sport's most explosive weapons in Malachi Toney, but also one of the most efficient passers in college football in Darian Mensah. I know Clemson is at home, but this has a chance to be a route for the Hurricanes. Give me Miami, big. Rob Gregson , A to Z Sports Alabama Miami 34, Clemson 21 This game is much closer than the final score suggests, with Clemson hanging around for a large portion of the afternoon. One of the biggest storylines will be how the Tigers handle Malachi Toney. It'll be interesting to see if Clemson allows CB Ashton Hampton to follow Toney around the field and essentially shadow him, considering Hampton is the most talented defensive back Miami has faced to this point. If Clemson can limit Toney and force Miami to win elsewhere, the Tigers have a chance to make this uncomfortable. Ultimately, though, Miami's overall talent takes over as the game progresses. The Hurricanes make enough explosive plays on offense to create separation, while Clemson capitalizes on a couple of coverage busts from the Miami secondary for some big plays of its own. Miami's depth and playmakers prove to be the difference in the second half, allowing the Hurricanes to pull away and finish with a 34-21 victory. Ryan Roberts , A to Z Sports Notre Dame Miami 30, Clemson 13 This feels like a game that could be closer than many pundits are giving it credit for, and perhaps those in Las Vegas as well. The 17-point line feels out of place for what Clemson has been over the last decade, but Dabo Swinney's Tigers have looked anything but the part of contenders the last few years. Clemson's secondary is talented, led by Ashton Hampton, who could play himself into first round consideration in April's NFL Draft. I could see the Tigers giving Miami's offense problems and preventing some of the chunk plays that Miami has ripped off all year with the exception of a quarter and a half against Wake Forest. But Clemson freshman QB Tait Reynolds is going to have a rough experience against a Miami team that's starting to get a tad healthier on the defensive side of the ball. DL Ahmad Moten, Sr. and Armondo Blount are off the injury report and appear set to be available on Saturday, along with CB Damari Brown. Starting CB Xavier Lucas could even possibly be in play, but even if not, Ethan O'Connor has been one of the better CBs in the ACC this year and can handle things very capably. Miami slowly puts this one away in the second half with Mark Fletcher, Jr., who is also off the injury report, pounding away in the fourth quarter on a tired defense. away.blurb: Week three’s road trip to Wake Forest decimated Miami’s health, losing backup running back Marty Brown (knee) and WR3 Joshua Moore (upper-body) for the season. Crucial starters in Ahmad Moten Sr., WR Malachi Toney, and RB Mark Fletcher all got banged up to a more limited extent. The position group most heavily impacted by injuries is the secondary with Frederique, Lucas, Ja’Boree Antoine out for extended periods with Damari Brown nicked up as well. While sophomore safety Bryce Fitzgerald theoretically plugs in well at corner due to his length and athleticism, it has been glaringly obvious that he is playing out of position so far this season. Fitzgerald referred to him as a “freak of nature” after his first four games, indicating that his expanded role is not likely to diminish even when the guys in front of him return. Sophomore wideout Malachi Toney is on pace for 102 catches, 1,700+ yards, and 18 touchdowns following his record-breaking freshman season. However, despite this elite production from the Heisman candidates, the offense has lost multiple weapons with Brown and Moore out for the season. The Hurricanes are lucky to have the two best statistical receivers in the country from a year ago in the same room, and need to maximize their talent. away.headline: Why the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes Should Limit Starters Returning From Injury
away.blurb: MIAMI, Fla. – After missing last Saturday's 52-3 win over Central Michigan at Hard Rock Stadium, the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes are set for the return of running back Mark Fletcher Jr. and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr. (both seniors) against Clemson , but it should be taken with caution. The backfield supporting cast suffered a difficult loss of redshirt junior CharMar "Marty" Brown, who is out for the rest of the season with a severe right knee injury, which was sustained against Wake Forest on Sept. 18. He was the primary backup to Fletcher Jr., but an opportunity for more snaps presents itself. For starters, Fletcher Jr. shouldn't return to a heavy workload. As the Hurricanes' go-to running back, the 21-year-old's long-term availability is valuable. Fletcher Jr. proved to turn things up a notch when the lights got brighter in last year's historic run to the National Championship game. Why the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes Should Limit Starters Returning From Injury - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Why the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes Should Limit Starters Returning From Injury (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Anthony Aguirre Wed, September 30, 2026 at 12:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As the Fort Lauderdale (Fla.) native is inserted back into the mix, it would be beneficial to make it an emphasis to play sophomore Girard Pringle Jr. , freshman Javian Mallory, and redshirt sophomore Chris Wheatley-Humphrey more. Plus, Pringle Jr., Mallory, and Wheatley-Humphrey can gain experience playing college football in a hostile environment. Memorial Stadium, otherwise known as Death Valley, is one of the sport's most historic venues. Pringle Jr. only logged six snaps in last year's College Football Playoffs and Wheatley-Humphrey had 19, but only on special teams. As Hurricanes offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson looks to spread the workload in the backfield, this Saturday presents an opportunity to play at least four different running backs. They will be facing Clemson 's junior linebacker, Sammy Brown , who was the ACC Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2024. Moten Sr. is off to a slow start this season. Thus far, in 91 snaps across three games, he's logged three total tackles, a solo and two assists, 0.5 tackles for loss, 0.5 sacks, and four pressures. Moten Sr. suffered a left shoulder injury against Wake Forest, left early, then returned to play the rest of the game. Despite having first-round projections in the 2027 NFL Draft, the Hurricanes still need the star defender healthy in the long run. It presents an opportunity for sophomore Jarquez Carter and junior Keona Davis, who have been serviceable in reserve roles, to step up. The Hurricanes have great depth at both running back and defensive tackle. away.headline: Miami injury report: Is Mark Fletcher playing vs Clemson?
away.blurb: News Sports Restaurants Real Estate Opinion Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals HURRICANES Miami injury report: Is Mark Fletcher playing vs Clemson? Dan Rorabaugh USA TODAY NETWORK - Florida Oct. 3, 2026, 9:01 a.m. ET The Miami football team has been battling injuries all season. But there's been good news coming out of Coral Gables leading up to a prime-time ACC test at Clemson . Fletcher, who led the ACC with 1,192 rushing yards with 14 total touchdowns in 2025 and leads the Hurricanes with 230 yards this year, sustained an upper-body injury that forced him to miss most of the fourth quarter in a tighter-than-expected victory against Wake. His health became even more important when No. 2 back Marty Brown was ruled out for the rest of the season after a knee injury earlier in the game. With Moten already out, Miami's other starting defensive tackle, Armondo Blount, got banged up vs. CMU. It was the latest in a string of injuries affecting the Canes' defense, down its two starting cornerbacks — O.J. Frederique and Xavier Lucas — since Week 1. Key backups Ja'Boree Antoine and Damari Brown have also been out, but despite the injuries, UM still fields the No. 2 defense in the nation by yards, No. 4 in points and No. 1 in rush yards. The following players have been ruled out: WR Joshua Moore (out for season), RB CharMar Brown (out for season), DB Ja'Boree Antoine, DB O.J. Frederique, TE Owen Ruskavich, TE Luka Gilbert (out for season). After sitting out last week's game against Central Michigan, running back Mark Fletcher was not on the injury report ahead of today's game at Clemson, signifying he is likely to play. If he is unavailable, Miami will split carries between Javian Mallory, Girard Pringle Jr. and Jordan Lyle with Chris Wheatley-Humphrey sprinked in. Clemson would lean its defense more on containing Malachi Toney and the passing game. Coach Mario Cristobal said running back Mark Fletcher and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten were held out against Central Michigan for precautionary reasons and that both were "ready to roll." Asked about the slew of defenders who missed or were injured during the CMU game, Cristobal said Sept. 28 that the biggest playmakers — Moten and fellow defensive tackle Armondo Blount — were good to go against Clemson. He also said cornerback Xavier Lucas, who was injured in the opener at Stanford and hasn't played since, could be back tonight. Lucas was listed as questionable as of Thursday night. Who benefits if Mark Fletcher is out vs Clemson? Top running back Mark Fletcher Jr. and run-stuffing defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr. were among those hurt Sept. 18 at Wake Forest. And while coach Mario Cristobal said the prognosis for both was positive in the week leading up to last week's home date with Central Michigan, both key players were on the sidelines without pads during the 52-3 win . The Hurricanes have been battling injuries all season , and in the last game against Central Michigan, many key starters were out for safety, giving others a chance to shine in their moment. home.headline: Dabo Swinney provides update on Christopher Vizzina injury, Clemson backup QB plan
home.blurb: Clemson quarterback Christopher Vizzina (right) injured his left elbow against Georgia Southern, but coach Dabo Swinney (left) said Vizzina will still be available vs. North Carolina. Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina is available, coach Dabo Swinney said, but not 100 percent recovered from a small fracture in his left elbow. What’s the Tigers’ plan if they need a backup to play vs. Miami? Clemson listed Vizzina as a game-time decision in the final availability report before Clemson’s Sept. 19 win over North Carolina. He was left off the final report entirely before the Sept. 25 win at Cal. He was listed as Clemson’s backup quarterback on the depth chart vs. Miami, per team release. Top Story Dabo Swinney provides update on Christopher Vizzina injury, Clemson backup QB plan By Jackson Castellano jcastellano@postandcourier.com Jackson Castellano Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said Vizzina is throwing and practicing after sustaining a small left elbow fracture Sept. 12 against Georgia Southern. However, Swinney said that Trent Pearman would be Clemson’s second option at quarterback vs. Miami if necessary. “He's still not 100 percent on his left arm, so if he plays, he plays with a brace on it to protect it,” Swinney said. “But it's really more just the range of motion for him, kind of getting that back fully. But it's gotten a little better each day.” Swinney said Vizzina could play in an emergency. He wasn’t listed in the initial ACC availability report Sept. 30. The senior has 14 completions for 102 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions this season. He was in the running for Clemson’s QB1 job with freshman Tait Reynolds during preseason camp, but Vizzina was ultimately named the starter in Week 1. Vizzina played three drives in the 22-7 win over Georgia Southern before Reynolds took over. The pair had previously split reps in a 51-10 loss to LSU. Reynolds was named the starter moving forward after the Georgia Southern game, but Swinney said the change had nothing to do with Vizzina’s health. In two career starts and four total games, Reynolds has thrown for 521 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Pearman, a fifth-year senior , joined Clemson as a walk-on in 2022. He has 10 passing attempts in his career, completing four for 43 yards. The D.W. Daniel graduate has played 33 career snaps. Reynolds will start for Clemson (3-1, 2-0 ACC) in its Oct. 3 matchup with No. 4 Miami (4-0, 2-0). Reach Jackson Castellano at jcastellano@po

home.headline: Miami Hurricanes update Xavier Lucas’ status for Clemson game
home.blurb: The Hurricanes on Friday downgraded Lucas from questionable to out, according to the latest availability report from the ACC on Friday. Miami (4-0, 2-0 ACC) has been playing without three of its top cornerbacks basically all season. Starters Lucas and OJ Frederique have out since sustaining undisclosed injuries during the season opener at Stanford, while sophomore reserve Ja’Boree Antoine has been out since before the season began. Meanwhile, linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin has been upgraded to probable after initially being listed as questionable. Hurricanes coach Mario Cristobal on Monday said Lucas was “getting closer” to returning to game action. In their absence, the trio of Ethan O’Connor, Damari Brown and safety Bryce Fitzgerald have been Miami’s primary outside cornerbacks. This story was originally published October 2, 2026 at 8:14 PM . home.blurb: Starting Clemson football left guard Elyjah Thurmon is listed as probable on the Tigers ' injury report Oct. 2 for their home game against No. 4 Miami . That's an upgrade from questionable on the first two reports. Thurmon left Clemson's 24-10 win over California on Sept. 25 with an injury. He didn't return, and sophomore Gavin Blanchard replaced him for the rest of the game. Swinney said that Vizzina is practicing and should be available against Miami , but that Pearman would be the next guy up after starter Tait Reynolds at the moment. Vizzina suited up against Cal . home.headline: What first Miami-Clemson availability report reveals about key Hurricanes injuries
home.blurb: Junior Xavier Lucas , who hasn't played since the season opener against Stanford , is listed as questionable for Saturday, according to the Atlantic Coast Conference's first availability report for the game released on Wednesday. Miami has been playing without three of its top cornerbacks basically all season, with starters Lucas and OJ Frederique out since the Stanford game and sophomore reserve Ja'Boree Antoine out since before the season began. Other players who sat out or were banged up against Central Michigan but don't appear on the availability report: running back Mark Fletcher Jr. , defensive linemen Ahmad Moten Sr. and Armondo Blount, and linebacker Kellen Wiley. Linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin is listed as questionable and reserve tight end Owen Ruskavich is out. As for Clemson, two players are listed as questionable (defensive end Armon Mason and Elyjah Thurmon), while seven have been ruled out (safety Polo Anderson, cornerback Shavar Young Jr., wide receiver Cole Turner , running back David Eziomume, defensive tackles Kourtney Kelly and Markus Strong, and offensive lineman Mason Wade). Hurricanes coach Mario Cristobal on Monday said Lucas was "getting closer" to returning to game action. "Not all the way there yet," Cristobal said. "Hopefully, good news later this week. There's been a lot of progress. Works his butt off, but not all the way there." In their absence, the trio of Ethan O'Connor, Damari Brown and safety Bryce Fitzgerald have been Miami's primary outside cornerbacks. Speaking of Brown, he did not play last week against Central Michigan but does not have an injury designation, signaling that he should be good to go against Clemson.
